summary.text: Steven St John, a no-party candidate and hospital chaplain in Las Vegas for nearly a decade, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Nevada's 1st Congressional District to Dina Titus.
He previously worked in advertising, marketing and business development and was a candidate in the 2014 election for another Nevada House seat.

paragraphs.text: St John earned a high school diploma from New Trier High School and a master's degree from San Diego State University, which Ballotpedia's education listing dates to 1976.

In his Ballotpedia survey he says he was self-employed as a young man, refinishing fences and doing home improvement work for neighbors, and that he experienced homelessness for several months in the early 1980s.

Ballotpedia reports that he worked in advertising, marketing and business development and as a chaplain. In his 2026 survey he describes about a decade as a hospital chaplain in Las Vegas and says he served as a chaplain under Mayor Goodman's faith initiative, ministering to people experiencing homelessness.

St John appeared on the November 2014 general-election ballot in Nevada's 3rd Congressional District as an independent, in a race won by incumbent Joe Heck over Erin Bilbray; the Nevada Independent notes that he ran in that district in 2014.
In his Ballotpedia survey St John said he was not a career politician and that his campaign was built on listening, trust and working together.
During the campaign, he said he was running on healthcare, housing and cost-of-living issues and on working across party lines.
He received 1.7% of the vote to Dina Titus's 59.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
